description: The clinician-facing calculator displays '95% CI x% to y%' beside a patient's risk with no statement of what the interval covers, while the function's own documentation said no interval was shown because mm_predict() does not produce one. Both halves of that were false. The interval is the standard error of the linear predictor on the probability scale, which mm_predict() documents as being for the model's estimate and NOT for the person: it excludes between-person variation and model-selection uncertainty. A clinician reading the calculator will take it as the range the patient's risk lies in. The README's own commitment is that an interval states what it rests on or why there is none.
reproduce: Read R/calculator.R:21 against R/calculator.R:136-140 and the interval argument of mm_predict().
expected: Either the displayed label carries the caveat, or the interval is withheld, consistent with the way mm_validate() withholds an interval it cannot justify and says why.
actual: Hardcoded '95% CI' label with no caveat; documentation denied the interval existed.
disposition_note: Owner decision: withhold the interval from the patient-facing display, keep the calculation. Removed from all three surfaces it reached, which is two more than this finding originally named: the ci-display text slot, the comparison list's bar and its printed range, and the three CSS rules that styled them (a leftover style invites the markup back). mm_predict(interval = TRUE) is untouched and still returns .lower/.upper; the calculator still receives them; each saved record still carries them, and the stored upper bound still sets the comparison list's common scale. No fitted model, point estimate or calculation was altered and no substitute interval was introduced. The disclaimer now names PARAMETER, ESTIMATED RISK and PREDICTION uncertainty separately. Four pre-existing tests asserted the old behaviour and were inverted rather than deleted, so the old coverage now guards against reintroduction.

description: Handed an mm_project, a specification and not a fit, these generics fall through to the .default method and return NULL or a summaryDefault instead of refusing. vcov(), nobs(), confint() and formula() do error. A silent NULL is what this package refuses everywhere else.
expected: An informative error naming the stage: a project specifies a model, mm_model() fits one.
actual: NULL for coef, fitted and residuals; a summaryDefault of 24 elements for summary.
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-accessors.R, block: a project is NOT refused by four of the generics (finding R-1)
disposition_note: Closing it means adding mm_project methods, which widens the public API, so it is the owner's call under specification rule 4. Today's behaviour is pinned by a test.

description: stats::confint() on the stored rms fit errors: it dispatches to confint.glm, begins profiling, and fails. No profile-likelihood interval is available for an lrm fit.
expected: Either a profile interval or a documented alternative.
actual: Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors, after 'Waiting for profiling to be done...'
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-accessors.R, block: confint is Wald, and says so, because the profile route errors
disposition_note: confint.mm_model computes Wald intervals from vcov() and documents the broken profile route as the reason, rather than substituting silently, which specification B3 forbids.

description: The fitted formula's response term is the package's internal recoded outcome, .mm_y, not the column named in mm_project(outcome=). A caller reading formula(model) sees a variable that is not in their data.
expected: Documentation stating that the response is a derived column and naming its source.
actual: .mm_y ~ age + bmi + sex, with no note
disposition_note: Documented in formula.mm_model. RE1.1 and RE1.3a still want it in the model documentation.

description: rms::lrm() leaves fitted.values empty, so stats::fitted() on the fit returns NULL and any method must choose a scale explicitly.
expected: A documented scale for fitted values.
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-accessors.R, block: fitted returns values on a stated scale, because rms returns none
disposition_note: scale = c(response, link), with the relationship between the two asserted through plogis.

description: autotest leaves state in the directory it runs in, so a later run against a mutated fixture in the same directory fails even when the fixture is valid.
reproduce: Run autotest_package twice in one directory, editing the package between runs.
expected: Each run independent of earlier runs in the same directory.
actual: Later runs fail; rebuilding the fixture in a fresh directory passes.
disposition_note: This caused a retracted conclusion during this work: an in-place bisect appeared to isolate the C-2 trigger and was measuring leftover state. Mitigation: a fresh fixture directory per autotest run.

description: Enumerating mysterynpi, a different repository, raises 'longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length' from a comparison inside autotest, call str_const_i > testthat_start, then halts with 'Test failures.'. Reproduced in a clean git worktree at a single function with test = FALSE, so no generated test has run. A minimal one-function package enumerates cleanly, so it is not a blanket tool failure.
reproduce: In a clean worktree of mysterynpi: autotest_package('.', functions = 'check_scalar', test = FALSE)
expected: Enumeration returns a data frame of candidate tests.
actual: Warning from autotest's own code, then 'Test failures.'
disposition_note: Probable test-tool defect triggered by a property of mysterynpi not yet isolated. The earlier narrowing was contaminated by C-1 and has been discarded. Not evidence about mysterymodel, which is a different repository.

function: saboteur: patient ids reshuffled is a different cohort
description: The precondition assertion used expect_setequal() on two table() results, which compares the counts as a set and ignores which identifier each count belongs to. testthat warns 'expect_setequal() ignores names'. The intent, stated in the comment above it, is that each identifier keeps its own visit count.
reproduce: Run the suite and read warning 10.
expected: An assertion that each identifier keeps its visit count.
actual: A set comparison of counts with identifiers discarded.
disposition_note: Changed to expect_identical, which is strictly stronger and passes. The saboteur detection itself was never in doubt: it is the expect_error on the following line, which asserts mm_validate() refuses the reshuffled cohort.

description: Called with a degenerate or all-NA axis, mm_risk_ticks() correctly returns a zero-length result, but emits base R's 'no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf' and the matching max warning on the way, because min() and max() are called on the empty or all-NA input without a guard. A documented behaviour path should not leak an implementation detail as a warning.
expected: A zero-length result with no warning.
actual: A zero-length result plus two base R warnings.
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-nomogram.R: expect_no_warning() on the all-NA and zero-length axis, plus expect_length(mm_risk_ticks(c(-Inf, Inf)), 0) and c(1, Inf) so the new guard cannot start accepting an infinite bound
disposition_note: Fixed by asking any(is.finite(lp_real)) before range(), one line, after a warning audit of the whole suite showed this was 2 of 10 unexplained warnings. The original range check is retained, so no return value changes for any input: verified by R CMD check Status OK with the suite's warning count falling 10 to 7 and no assertion changing its result.

location: tests/testthat/test-calculator.R, 'the form opens on the cohort's most ordinary member'
description: The block sabotaged the fit with broken$datadist$limits["Adjust to", "site"] <- "vanished" to check that an Adjust-to value absent from the schema falls back. Assigning an unknown level into a factor cell stores NA and warns, so the test exercised the is.na(typical) branch of mm_calculator_defaults() while its comment claimed the !typical %in% levels branch. Both branches return the same value, so the test passed and the gap was visible only as an unexplained warning in the suite.
reproduce: Delete the '!typical %in% specs[[p]]$levels' clause from R/calculator.R:613-614 and run the calculator tests
expected: The test fails, because the not-in-levels branch is what it claims to cover.
actual: FAIL 0: the mutant survived, since the cell held NA and the is.na() branch still returned levels[1].
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-calculator.R: the column is coerced to character before the assignment so "vanished" actually lands, and the NA case is kept as its own assertion
disposition_note: Red-first evidence recorded in both directions with the mutation's diff printed before each run: old test + mutant = FAIL 0 (survived); corrected test + mutant = FAIL 1, 'actual: "vanished", expected: "rare"'. A first attempt at this mutation used perl \Q, which silently did not apply the edit and would have scored a meaningless pass; the applied diff is printed for that reason.

location: R/calculator.R, the numeric branch of mm_calculator_defaults()
description: The categorical branch refused an "Adjust to" value the schema did not recognise and fell back to the first level; the numeric branch returned whatever datadist$limits held, unchecked. The schema's range is built from the rows the model was fitted on and datadist from what it was given, so the two can disagree -- the same schema-versus-filtering family as M09. A disagreement meant the calculator opened on a value outside the developed range, i.e. already extrapolating, and a missing one opened the form on a blank field. test-calculator.R asserts the in-range property but only for an uncorrupted fit, so nothing covered the asymmetry.
reproduce: fit <- mm_model(...); fit$datadist$limits["Adjust to", "age"] <- 1e6; mm_calculator_defaults(fit)$age, against a schema range of 18-95
expected: A default inside the developed range, as the categorical branch already guaranteed for levels.
actual: 1e+06, and mm_predict() on those defaults then flags .extrapolated = TRUE for the patient the form opens on. With NA it returned NA and mm_predict() errored on a missing predictor.
verification_test: tests/testthat/test-adversarial-defaults-and-ticks.R: 'a numeric default is inside the range the model was developed on' and 'whatever datadist holds, the form opens on a scorable patient'
disposition_note: Out-of-range clamps to the nearer bound, so the opening value stays as close to the fit's own adjust-to as the range permits; non-finite or non-numeric falls back to the midpoint of the developed range. PRESENTATION CHOICE FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER: the midpoint is in range by construction but is not the cohort median and should not be read as one. The alternative was to error on an inconsistent fitted object, which would stop the app starting. Found while writing adversarial tests for W-2 and W-3, not reported by any tool. Red-first evidence: mutation MW4 in review/mutation-evidence.csv, 24 assertion failures with the diff printed before the run.
